review_notes: Read the whole target file and compared its norm-bound proof with the near-identical proofs in RegularisedBesselLinearTensorPath.lean (two copies, norm_le and difference_norm_le) and RegularisedComplexLinearVolterraUniqueness.lean (hDweight). I did not check the other declarations in the target (def, continuity, sub). Continuity is a one-line comp₂, and the sub lemma is a simp, so neither is a repeated-machinery issue. The line numbers for the norm_le theorem are derived from the file text. The suggested lemma has not been compiled. Its gcongr proof needs ‖F‖ ≥ 0, ‖x‖ ≥ 0 and B ≥ 0, which I expect to follow from norm_nonneg and hx. The residual risk is that the per-use saving is modest.

findings.problem: The proof of the pointwise bound ‖F x y‖ ≤ C * B * ‖y‖ is a hand-written chain: le_opNorm₂, then ‖F‖ ≤ C and ‖x‖ ≤ B, with the nonnegativity side conditions, then ‖y‖ ≤ ‖v‖. It is done with h1/h2/trans/mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_*, and it is copied almost verbatim in at least three other places. These are regularisedBesselLinearTensorPath_norm_le and regularisedBesselLinearTensorPath_difference_norm_le (both in RegularisedBesselLinearTensorPath.lean) and hDweight in RegularisedComplexLinearVolterraUniqueness.lean. The only differences are the map, the constant and the target space. Nothing about the argument is specific to the regularised tensor, so any fix or simplification must be repeated in each copy.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one generic lemma, e.g. in a shared Leray utility file or at the top of this file:

theorem opNorm₂_apply_le_of_bounds {𝕜 E₁ E₂ G} [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup E₁] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E₁] [NormedAddCommGroup E₂] [NormedSpace 𝕜 E₂] [NormedAddCommGroup G] [NormedSpace 𝕜 G] (F : E₁ →L[𝕜] E₂ →L[𝕜] G) {C B : ℝ} (hF : ‖F‖ ≤ C) {x : E₁} (hx : ‖x‖ ≤ B) (y : E₂) : ‖F x y‖ ≤ C * B * ‖y‖.

Proof sketch: calc ‖F x y‖ ≤ ‖F‖ * ‖x‖ * ‖y‖ := F.le_opNorm₂ _ _, then `_ ≤ C * B * ‖y‖ := by gcongr`. The side goals 0 ≤ ‖F‖, 0 ≤ ‖x‖ and 0 ≤ B are closed by norm_nonneg and (norm_nonneg x).trans hx.

Rewritten use in regularisedComplexLinearTensorPath_norm_le, with q := regularizedMildTimeClamp T hT s: `change ‖F (g q) (v q)‖ ≤ _; exact (opNorm₂_apply_le_of_bounds F (regularisedTensorPhysicalMap_norm_le ρ ε hε).2 (hg q) (v q)).trans (mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (v.norm_coe_le_norm q) (mul_nonneg hC hB))`. This uses the existing hypotheses hg, hB and hC, and the imports are unchanged.

Rewritten use in the Bessel difference lemma: the same lemma applied to (v q - w q), followed by `simpa using (v - w).norm_coe_le_norm q`. The Volterra hDweight uses it with y := (u - v) q and the bound hweightPoint.
findings.benefit: The h1/h2 monotonicity argument and its nonnegativity bookkeeping would be stated and proved once instead of in four places. Each caller would reduce to supplying the operator bound, the pointwise bound on g, and the sup-norm bound on v. That makes the intended estimate ‖F‖·‖g‖·‖v‖ readable and keeps the Bessel, complex-physical and Volterra variants consistent when constants or hypotheses change.
